seoTitle: How to Export Asana Data to Excel Easily
metaDescription: See how to export Asana project data to Microsoft Excel in 2026, downloading a CSV file and importing it while keeping columns and dates intact.
intro: Building custom reports or archiving a finished project often means getting your Asana data into Excel, and the process runs through a straightforward CSV export. This guide covers exporting from the List view, importing the file into Excel, and cleaning up formatting so dates and text display correctly.

steps.heading: Switch to the List view
steps.body: Open your active Asana project and switch to the List view, which is the layout the export tool reads from.

steps.heading: Open the export menu
steps.body: Access the project dropdown header menu to locate the export settings option.

steps.heading: Export as CSV
steps.body: Select the Export CSV option and save the file to your device.

steps.heading: Open the file in Excel
steps.body: Launch Microsoft Excel, open a blank workbook, and use the data import tool to parse the CSV so columns align correctly.

steps.heading: Adjust formatting
steps.body: Fix column widths, text formats, and date fields as needed, then save the file as an official Excel Workbook for reporting.

faq.question: Will custom field values be included in the export?
faq.answer: Yes, custom field values along with assignees and due dates are included in the exported task list.

faq.question: Why do my dates look wrong after importing into Excel?
faq.answer: This typically happens when Excel misreads the date format from the CSV, so use the import tool's column formatting step to set date fields explicitly.

faq.question: Can I export a project with hundreds of tasks?
faq.answer: Yes, the CSV export handles large projects, though very large files may take a moment to generate and download.

faq.question: Does exporting to CSV remove data from Asana?
faq.answer: No, exporting only creates a copy of your data as a file; nothing is deleted or changed inside your Asana project.
